learningObjective: Explain the roles of Dialect, Trait, and Interface in MLIR extensibility, and identify what each entity does and does not do.
stem: Which of the following statements about MLIR Dialects, Traits, and Interfaces are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A Trait is compile-time metadata attached to an Op class that Pass writers can query with a static check (e.g., `SameOperandsAndResultType`, `MemoryEffects`), letting analyses and rewrites treat many Ops uniformly.
An Interface is a virtual method table on Ops (or Dialects/Types), letting client code call polymorphic behavior on an Op without knowing its concrete class (e.g., `InferShapedTypeOpInterface`).

Once an Op is defined in one Dialect, it can never be aliased into another Dialect; therefore lowering between Dialects always requires cloning the Op and rebuilding all its uses from scratch, without leveraging any interface polymorphism.
A Dialect is a registration namespace grouping related Operations, Types, and Attributes; different Dialects can coexist in one IRModule, enabling progressive lowering across levels of abstraction.

explanation: Options A, B, D are correct; option C is incorrect. A (Correct): Traits are static compile-time metadata for uniform handling. B (Correct): Interfaces are virtual method dispatch on Ops/Types/Dialects. C (Wrong): dialect conversion + patterns replace Ops using rewriter APIs; interfaces enable polymorphic legalization. D (Correct): Dialects group ops/types/attrs and can coexist for progressive lowering.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: Traits are static compile-time metadata for uniform handling.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: Interfaces are virtual method dispatch on Ops/Types/Dialects.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: dialect conversion + patterns replace Ops using rewriter APIs; interfaces enable polymorphic legalization.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: Dialects group ops/types/attrs and can coexist for progressive lowering.

assumptions: The reader is thinking about MLIR core extensibility mechanisms, not any downstream project's naming.
nonImplications: Does not imply that Traits and Interfaces are interchangeable; Traits are static, Interfaces are virtual.
Does not imply every Dialect defines Types; some dialects only add Ops on top of built-in Types.

distractorRationales.C: Fabricates a 'clone-from-scratch' constraint; dialect conversion is the intended mechanism.
